text:
jia: heads-up — seeing steady VRAM growth on long-context workloads on T4s but not on H100s. reproduction attached below.

jia: traffic: chat-bot load, avg seq_len 6k tokens, sustained 30s+ sessions. on T4 worker VRAM climbs ~2GB per session over 60s, eventually OOM. H100 cluster steady.

andre: can you paste the kvcache counters / evict logs? is eviction happening but not freeing PT entries?

jia: paste logs from run: 
```
[2026-03-18T14:02:01Z] kvcache: total_slots=524288 used=398120 free=126168
[2026-03-18T14:02:31Z] kvcache: evict_attempts=2438 evicted=0 reclaimable_shadow=1987
[2026-03-18T14:03:01Z] pagetable: active_entries=412000 leaked_shadow=1900
[2026-03-18T14:03:31Z] gpu-mem: used=11.2GB -> 13.3GB
```

jia: note evicted=0 despite evict_attempts > 2k. reclaimable_shadow ticks up.

tess: interesting. i ran microprofile on both T4 and H100. T4 shows high stall in `pt_unmap()` where we try to dec refcount and free but loop spins on CAS. H100 shows happy fast path.

tess: snippet from profiler (flame): 
```
pt_unmap (55%) -> atomic_dec_loop (40%) -> sync_wait (15%)
```

andre: could be 32-bit vs 64-bit atomic differences / memory ordering on sm architecture. T4 uses older sm (Turing) that has different atomics semantics for 64-bit fetch_sub in device code. if refcounts are 64-bit but we do non-atomic 32-bit ops in some path, that would leak.

sam: also check kernel selection: we recently added warp-cooperative free kernel for H100 only (fast path). on T4 we fall back to scalar kernel that runs slower and retries. maybe the fallback has a bug.

andre: good call. @tess can you dump the kernel variants used and kernel launch params for the failing run?

tess: pasted kernel metadata: 
```
kfree_variant: fallback_scalar_v2 (sm_75) args= (ptr, count=1024)
kfree_variant: warp_fast_v1 (sm_90+) args=(ptr, count=1024)
```

tess: fallback_scalar_v2 does `while(!atomicCAS(&entry->owner, expected, 0)) { backoff(); }` and then `entry->state = FREE` — suspect path where expected computed incorrectly when concurrent reuse happens.

andre: that `expected` computation rings a bell — we compute expected = owner | FLAG_PINNED sometimes, and if reuse toggles low bits we may spin forever. different GPU memory ordering could make CAS never match in practice.

sam: quick workaround: add a timeout to scalar free to force reclaim and record diagnostics. if that stabilizes memory, we can ship a hotfix.

perf-bot: perf alert: kvcache regression detected on T4 e2e test (peak mem +18% in last 48h). see run 2026-03-18_14:00.

infra-bot: repro machines: t4-4 (driver 510.47), h100-2 (driver 545.34). kernel build sha: a1b2c3d. rolling a test job to try `scalar_free_timeout=1ms`.

jia: tried `scalar_free_timeout=1ms` locally — growth flattened, sessions ran 2x longer without hitting OOM. not ideal but actionable.

andre: plan: (1) add guard/timeout + counters for scalar free, (2) write microtest that stresses simultaneous unmap+remap across threads to reproduce CAS mismatch, (3) evaluate using 32-bit vs 64-bit atomics consistency. i'll take (1) and (2).

tess: i'll prepare profiling artifacts and a small repro script (node loadgen + longctx prompt). will attach perf traces.

sam: and i'll run the variant where we force warp_free on T4 (emulate fast path) to see if problem goes away — if yes, that's a strong hint it's kernel implementation, not page table invariants.

jia: thanks all. tagging for triage: @andre please add to kvcache bugboard and assign priority P1 for Dedicated clusters affecting prod T4 pools. :warning:

andre: done — created bug #IR-1247 with steps, logs, and temp workaround. assigning to eng-runtime kvcache owners.

jia: if anyone wants fast repro: start `loadgen longctx --seq 6k --concurrency 8 --duration 10m --target t4-4`

sam: logging note: add `kvcache.debug=owner_cas_fail` print for 10s when threshold exceeded so we don't spam logs long-term.

perf-bot: regression ticket linked: IR-1247. next: rerun e2e mem profile after scalar timeout patch.
